title: Rails transactional outbox: save intent with the change
outcome: Close the DB/publish loss gap while accepting and handling duplicate publication.
useCase: Reliable Rails facts consumed by other services.
benefits: No lost publication intent after a committed business change.
drawbacks: Dispatcher operations and duplicate handling remain.
version: Kafka 4.1 KRaft · lab Ruby 3.3 / Rails 7.2 · legacy Rails adaptation notes
cue: Commit the fact and its intent together. Publish later. Expect repeats.

trace.title: Trusted completion command
trace.detail: A direct DB write followed by a Kafka send is a dual write. Crash after DB commit but before send loses the event. Send first and a later DB rollback can publish a fact that never committed. Neither ordering solves both cases.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
HTTP completion → lock/check → ticket update + outbox insert → DB commit → dispatcher reads → producer delivery acknowledgement → published mark. Break the process at each arrow and state what can be retried.

after_commit enqueue alone still has a crash gap. It can be useful as a wake-up, but a durable scanner/outbox source must recover missing wake-ups.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Holding a DB lock during a slow network send can hurt capacity. Multiple dispatchers can reorder or duplicate without a deliberate claim strategy. A published flag is evidence of a local mark, not downstream completion.
